description_full: Rogers Communications Inc. operates as a communications, sports, and entertainment company in Canada. It operates through Wireless, Cable, and Media segments. The company offers mobile internet access, wireless voice and enhanced voice, device financing, device protection, global voice and data roaming, wireless home phone, bridging landline, machine-to-machine and Internet of Things solutions, and advanced wireless solutions for businesses, as well as device shipping and pickup services; satellite-to-mobile service; and wireless solutions under the Rogers, Fido, and chatr brands. It also provides Internet access, Internet protocol-based (IP) television, applications, online viewing, phone, home monitoring, and advanced home WiFi services to consumer and businesses. In addition, the company offers local and network TV; on-demand television; cloud-based digital video recorders; voice-activated remote controls, restart, and integrated apps; linear and time-shifted programming; digital specialty channels; and 4K television programming. Further, it provides residential and small business local telephony services; voicemail, call waiting, and long distance; video and audio programming; voice, data networking, IP, and Ethernet services; private networking, Internet, IP voice, and cloud solutions; optical wave and multi-protocol label switching services; information technology and network technologies; cable access network services; telecommunications technical consulting services; and season games through television, smartphones, tablets, personal computers, and other streaming devices. Additionally, the company owns Toronto Blue Jays and the Rogers Centre event venue; and operates Sportsnet ONE, Sportsnet 360, Sportsnet World, Citytv, OMNI, FX (Canada), FXX (Canada), and HGTV television networks, as well as AM and FM radio stations. It also offers Rogers and the Rogers Red World Elite Mastercard. The company was founded in 1960 and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

financial_summary: Rogers Communication, Inc. is a large-cap communication services business with a $18.0B market cap on $15.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 7% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $1.6B in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.88× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.6× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.8×.

Shareholder yield of 3.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 11% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.2× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 15% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 19% below the high.

val: The stock trades 79% below its blended-model fair value of $156, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 76%), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Communication Services peers: cheaper on EV/EBITDA 7.1 vs 9.4, richer on P/E 28.7 vs 14.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 42% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 8.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 10.3% (vs the 8% bar).

It converts 10% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 39% is amplified by 5.1x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.6x net debt to EBITDA ($951.3M of cash against $28.2B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 4.8x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.75 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.61 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.5% over 3 years and 8.4% over 5 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 1.0% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 3.2% on average.
Analysts expect -1.8% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 10.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 68%.
It returns 3.6% a year to shareholders (4.3% in dividends).
It pays out 118% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 25,000 employees, each generates about $615K of revenue, in line with the Communication Services median, and productivity has risen 4.5% a year.
That works out to $62K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.6M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
